hypothesis_card.mechanism: Recent-window (180d) empirical h-day log-change quantiles track the prevailing drift regime (2023-24: rising AI demand, measured recent-180d h180 q50 +0.65 vs 730d 0.0 at 2024-09), and AZs priced below their instance-type cross-sectional median revert upward (corr +0.57 at h180). Both shift the whole quantile triple up, reducing the -0.30 h180 center bias and the 34% q90 breach that dominate the pooled loss.
hypothesis_card.expected_observation: Discovery pooled skill rises from 0.2450 to ~0.273 with the h180 slice improving most (+0.051 skill, coverage +0.008) and h90 slightly (+0.008); h30 unchanged (gated). Dense backtest shows h180 +0.040 skill with the p5 (H100) series most helped and no horizon regressing.
hypothesis_card.competing_explanation: The gain is not regime adaptation but pure variance reduction from averaging two noisy quantile estimates (730d and 180d windows), which would also appear when blending two arbitrary windows and would not be specific to the rising-demand regime; alternatively the 2023-24 Discovery uptrend makes ANY upward center shift look good in-sample while adding no out-of-sample information (the champion's center is in-sample-optimal by construction).
hypothesis_card.test: Paired comparison vs the seed champion on the 16 Discovery origins (dry run) and a dense 33-origin stride-14 backtest inside Discovery, decomposing per-horizon deltas: the blend-only backtest isolated the recent-window lever (h180 +0.040, h30 -0.012) and the dry run isolated the CS-shift contribution (h90 -0.015 -> +0.008 with shift on), which motivated the h>=90 gate.
hypothesis_card.rejection_condition: Rejected if Discovery pooled skill <= champion (0.2450) or any sanity check fails; the regime hypothesis is falsified if the h180 gain disappears out of sample (Holdout h180 skill <= champion's 0.3551) or if the recent-window blend is loss-positive at h90/h180 on the dense backtest (it was +0.040 at h180, -0.015 at h90 before gating).

hypothesis: At 30/90/180-day horizons AWS GPU spot prices are regime-driven (AI demand build-out vs capacity ramp), so the seed's fixed 730-day pooled change quantiles are stale: measured mean bias is -0.03/-0.16/-0.30 (log) at h30/90/180 with q90 breach 27%. Blending recent-180d change quantiles (w=0.5) and adding a capped cross-sectional mean-reversion shift (AZs below their instance-type median revert up; corr(fwd, csmed-level) = +0.26/+0.44/+0.57) at h>=90 only raises the center and upper band into the prevailing regime, cutting the long-horizon bias and q90 breaches. Both levers are gated OFF at h30, where the dense backtest showed them loss-negative (-0.012/-0.055).
market_insight: The forecast assumes AWS GPU spot prices over 30-180 days are driven by the generative-AI capacity cycle rather than short-term momentum: H100 (p5) demand outstripping supply keeps a positive drift on premium instances, while older-generation A100 (p4d) capacity gradually migrates to H100/H200 fleets, leaving AZ-level discounts to mean-revert toward the instance-type median. Dated evidence from point-in-time searches: Liftr Insights (2024-05-29, prnewswire.com/news-releases/ai-accelerator-prices-rising-but-its-good-for-users-302157388.html) verifies a 12.2% 3-year rise in AI cloud compute prices; Shadeform (2024-01-20, shadeform.com/resources/articles/nvidia-a100-gpus-a-cost-and-availability-analysis) documents Lambda Labs' largest price increase and the A100-to-H100 market shift; Aaron Ginn (2024-02-07, linkedin.com/pulse/month-gpus-february-2024) notes H100 prices stabilizing after 2023's increase with supply shortages easing; TechCrunch (2024-05-05) and NextPlatform (2024-05-02) document hyperscaler H100 allocations (AWS ~50K) and alternative-cloud price pressure. A web-news drift gate built on these signals was tested and never fired on Discovery (all age-gated articles were direction-mixed), so the committed forecast is pack-only; the regime signal is captured instead by the recent-180d empirical change quantiles. The view would change if forward prices fell while the recent window showed gains (capacity build-out catching up, e.g. broad H200/GB200 availability or a demand shock), or if AZ-level dispersion stopped reverting (persistent regional allocation shifts).
